brief: GS's Fins & REITs daily opens with a market recap: financials underperformed (S&P Financial Index -0.72%), Treasury yields rose across the curve, VIX and the MOVE index rose, Bitcoin fell, and IG/HY CDX tightened. Robinhood's October metrics were mixed: net deposits rose to about $15bn, a 46% annualized growth rate that beat the company's 20% net-new-asset guidance (boosted by Trump Accounts), and new accounts and margin balances also rose. Against that, crypto volumes fell sharply month over month and year over year, securities lending revenue stayed negative for a third straight quarter, and platform assets fell 3%. GS's investment banks team calls the non-M&A advisory outlook, especially restructuring, constructive, says M&A stays mid-cycle, and prefers EVR, LCLN, PIPR, PJT for continued non-M&A growth. STAG and Weyerhaeuser gave operating updates on leasing pace/rent growth and lumber/OSB pricing. The macro section (GIR's 2027 outlook) argues the headline forecast, stable growth, falling inflation, peaking policy rates, is friendly, but flags late-cycle strain: higher real rates, wider credit spreads, rising volatility, and an AI impulse that has supported markets this year now poised to peak.
